purpose: Gate-bar self-check of the CV-1101 date-time gate. generated.points has one entry per mutation point enumerated from the AST of pm_event_datetime, pm_event_datetime_inventory and pm_event_datetime_value_probe (families in generated.families): a witness that the mutant makes fail, or a declared survivor with its reason. mutations are hand-written single edits, one per behaviour rule at least, each naming its rule and witness. rules are owner-derived predicates; statements has one row per owner statement (owner_text), naming the rules it states or why no mutation applies. A witness is check:<pm_event_datetime_selfcheck name> or case:<date-time corpus case id>. python3 scripts/pm_event_datetime_mutations.py --self-test checks freshness; --mutations replays every mutant.

families.refusal_site: Every way the date-time code emits a refusal: each raise statement, each _refuse(...) call, each call to a local error sink (a nested function that appends to errors: fail, unsupported), each error record (a dict literal with an "error" key), each errors.extend, each error-code tuple a function returns, each "status": "fail" constant, and each withholding call of the value probe (dependencies.append, unproven.add, dialects.update, dynamic.update), which records a reason to withhold credit. The mutant disables that one site: a raise becomes pass, a call becomes None, the list or comprehension holding an error record becomes [], an error tuple becomes (), and "fail" becomes "pass", and a withholding call becomes None.
families.refusal_predicate: Every predicate of an if or conditional-expression guard of a refusal site (each enclosing guard up to the function, the else branch included with the opposite polarity) where dropping that predicate alone makes the refusal fire less often: an or-operand that leads to the refusal becomes False, an and-operand that prevents it becomes True, and an element of a literal tuple scanned by any()/all() or tested with in/not in is dropped.
families.credit_predicate: Every predicate of the guard of a credit site, and of the value of a credit assignment, where dropping that predicate alone grants the credit more often. Credit sites are the committed credit names: deciding_nodes and timestamp_only_nodes entries, the static, all_refused, automatic, credited and on_value_path assignments of the value probe, and the used.add exemption of the scan.
families.comparison_boundary: Every <, <=, > and >= in the date-time code. The mutant flips strictness (< and <=, > and >=), the off-by-one at that range or limit boundary.

rules_source: Predicate-level rules derived from the owner rows. Each lists generated point keys and hand-written mutation ids; every one must be caught with its witness failing. Declared survivors are never listed.

rules.rule: The whole string is validated against the RFC 3339 5.6 grammar; any other character, a trailing LF or a prefix match refuses (date_time_syntax).
Only an exact str is a timestamp value; any other type, a str subclass included, refuses (date_time_type).
The year has exactly four digits.
Month 01..12; 00 and 13 refuse (date_time_month).
A real day of that month in the proleptic Gregorian calendar (date_time_day).
T or t separates date and time; a space refuses.
Hour 00..23 (date_time_hour).
Minute 00..59 (date_time_minute).
Second 00..59, or 60 only as a real leap second (date_time_second).
An optional fraction of one or more decimal digits with no digit ceiling; it is never rounded.
Z, z or a signed hh:mm offset is required; a missing zone refuses.
Offset hour 00..23 and minute 00..59 (date_time_offset_hour, date_time_offset_minute).
Second 60 is admitted only at a real leap second after applying the complete signed offset to the instant (date_time_leap_second).
The leap-second table is the IERS Bulletin C72 insertion history through 2016-12-31; no month-end guess, no later insertion without an edition update.
Year 0000 and the Gregorian century rules are handled without a narrower host date range.
The predicate returns the original string unchanged: case, zone spelling and every fractional digit.
A profile is selected only as one of the four owner profiles, passed as an exact str; anything else refuses (date_time_profile).
The default event_record profile admits lowercase t/z, offsets, legitimate leap seconds and arbitrary fractions.
storage_utc_z admits only a terminal uppercase Z; nonzero offsets, +00:00, -00:00 and lowercase z refuse (date_time_utc_z).
coordination_utc_z requires a trailing uppercase Z, for its owner fields only.
legacy_normalization_output requires exactly nine fractional digits and a trailing uppercase Z (date_time_legacy_fraction, date_time_utc_z).
No universal Z-only or nine-digit input restriction: the stricter profiles apply only where selected.
The format checker explicitly registers the CV-1101 predicate for date-time, raising its Refusal, under the selected profile.
format applies only to strings; a non-string passes the format check (type stays independent).
datetime_validator passes the registered checker for the selected profile to the validator it constructs.
The enforced validator composes the CV-253 terminal-Z constraint on the Storage fields of every Storage-classified node.
Composition applies to observed_at_utc and persisted_at_utc only, as classified in the inventory row.
The field boundary stays installed when a referenced resource declares $schema.
Composition keeps the original schema objects and every existing schema predicate.
Resource admission runs before every evaluated schema object, through descend as well as iter_errors.
Only a closed, preloaded Registry is accepted; any retrieve callback is refused before it runs, and a missing resource is never retrieved.
Custom resolver and _resolver configurations are refused.
Every supplied URI and embedded resource is pinned; an absent URI, a changed fingerprint, a conflicting URI or a removed classified target refuses.
A schema override of an admitted validator is refused.
Only draft 2020-12, 2019-09, draft-07 and draft-06 are selected; any other declared dialect refuses; no declaration means 2020-12.
A schema object declaring either field without an inventory classification raises DatetimeAdmissionError.
Runtime selections are built only from a validated inventory; an invalid inventory refuses (datetime_inventory_invalid).
The scan covers every regular file under Plans/, any suffix or case, following file and directory symlinks; cycles and broken symlinks fail.
UTF-8/16/32 JSON, JSON Unicode escapes, CommonMark fences and JSON-shaped inline code are decoded before classification.
Duplicate keys, unreadable declaration regexes and propertyNames, unreadable candidates and a missing CommonMark parser fail closed.

Non-timestamp credit needs a static closure: every reachable node 2020-12 with no other dialect at or above it, and no dynamic-scope keyword.

statements_source: One row per statement of the owner text selected in owner_text: every sentence of CV-1101's canonical_text, acceptance_criteria and negative_constraints, and of the adoption guide's date-time blocks (exactly the blocks the number rules table excludes as date-time owned; FIX11's final rule and the rules of FIX12-FIX15 are committed in the Shared calls block 'Before any runtime installation'). Keyed by source path, line and exact text.

statements.statement: This newly authored technical owner unit binds the existing EventRecord envelope date_time_string format: date-time to an enforced RFC 3339 section 5.6 date-time predicate, with section 5.7 calendar and leap-second restrictions.
It is owned by EventRecord/CV-317, independently of CV-1100's number-input grammar.
statements.no_mutation: Ownership or governance statement; no date-time code implements it.

statements.statement: Validate the entire string: four-digit Gregorian year, real month/day, T or t separator, hour 00..23, minute 00..59, second 00..59 or a legitimate second 60, optional fraction with one or more decimal digits and no general digit ceiling, then Z/z or a signed hh:mm offset with hour 00..23 and minute 00..59.
Missing zone, space separator, trailing LF, invalid calendar/range/offset and an illegitimate leap second refuse.
Lowercase t/z and nonzero offsets remain owner-valid for occurred_at_utc and broad family ts fields.
CV-253 binds Storage-assigned observed_at_utc and persisted_at_utc to the storage_utc_z profile: UTC with a terminal uppercase Z only; nonzero offsets, +00:00, -00:00 and lowercase z refuse.
The enforced EventRecord validator composes CV-253 constraints on only these two fields, combining the original schema and enforced date-time predicate with the terminal-Z restriction.
Composition preserves the pinned envelope schema bytes and every existing schema predicate; it does not restamp a registry resource hash.
This profile retains arbitrary fractional precision and legitimate UTC leap seconds; it adds no universal nine-digit input requirement.
Second 60 is admitted only at a real announced leap second after mathematically applying the complete signed offset to the represented instant; a local month-end check is insufficient.
Frozen validator resources include their authoritative leap-second data edition.

The reference predicate pins the IERS Bulletin C72 insertion history through 2016-12-31; later announced insertions require the applicable resource/edition update rather than guessing from a clock or treating every June/December boundary as a leap second.
Four-digit year 0000 and Gregorian century rules are handled without a narrower host datetime range.
Preserve every original timestamp string, case, zone spelling and all fractional digits in identity/hash preimages.
statements.note: Identity and hash preimages belong to their own owners; the date-time code's part is returning the string unchanged.

statements.statement: Validation never rewrites timestamps, rounds a fraction, converts to floating epoch seconds or truncates to microseconds.
Exact instant comparisons remain with their existing owners and compare offsets mathematically and complete fractional values.
statements.no_mutation: Exact instant comparison stays with its existing owners; the date-time code compares no instants.

statements.statement: Stricter local profiles remain selectable only where their existing field owners require them.
The coordination record timestamp profile requires trailing uppercase Z; do not impose that restriction on every envelope timestamp.

Legacy normalization's exactly nine fractional digits and trailing uppercase Z are its output form, not the current envelope input grammar; excess precision is never rounded merely to manufacture that output.
No existing local profile, hash recipe, schema range or field is replaced here.
statements.note: Hash recipes and schema ranges of other owners are outside the date-time code.

statements.statement: Install and pass the actual date-time predicate to validation.

The shared reference helper supplies an explicitly registered jsonschema format checker and a validator constructor that passes it; merely constructing FormatChecker(), or relying on a format annotation, is insufficient.
Negatives must demonstrate that the installed predicate runs through the validator.
Every lane adopts this check at its timestamp boundaries using the relevant existing owner profile, not a new local regex.
statements.no_mutation: An obligation of each adopting lane at its own boundaries; no shared date-time code implements it.

statements.note: SP-1101 original selection is RetainedDispatcher in pm_event_numbers (number scope, its own rules table); the date-time code supplies only the profiles it selects, whose rules are profile.*.

statements.no_mutation: Ownership or governance statement; no date-time code implements it.

statements.statement: Enforced source/family validator accepts valid lowercase, offsets, real offset-adjusted leap seconds and long fractions without rewriting strings.
Storage observed_at_utc and persisted_at_utc accept uppercase-Z UTC and refuse offsets including signed zero offsets and lowercase z under CV-253.
Missing zone, space, LF, invalid day/hour/offset and false leap seconds refuse through the registered format predicate.
Coordination Z-only and legacy normalization output checks are selected only for their existing owner contexts.
Authentic retained profiles preserve exact original timestamp spelling; forged profile selections and invalid originals refuse.
statements.note: SP-1101 original selection is RetainedDispatcher in pm_event_numbers (number scope, its own rules table); the date-time code supplies only the profiles it selects, whose rules are profile.*.

statements.statement: No universal Z-only or nine-digit input restriction; no timestamp normalization in hashes.
No caller-selected historical profile, skipped format enforcement, new family admission or native proof.
statements.note: SP-1101 original selection is RetainedDispatcher in pm_event_numbers (number scope, its own rules table); the date-time code supplies only the profiles it selects, whose rules are profile.*. Family admission and native proof are outside the date-time code.

statements.statement: Validate timestamp fields with `pm_event_datetime.datetime_validator` (the explicitly registered checker is passed), or call `date_time` at a separately enforced boundary.
The default `event_record` profile admits RFC3339 lowercase, offsets, legitimate leap seconds and arbitrary fractional precision for `occurred_at_utc` and broad family `ts` fields.

CV-253 requires the separate `storage_utc_z` profile for Storage-assigned `observed_at_utc`/`persisted_at_utc`: terminal uppercase `Z` only, refusing nonzero, `+00:00`, `-00:00` and lowercase-`z` zones without limiting fractional digits.
Construct `datetime_validator` at the complete outer validation boundary and pass the authentic schema resources as `registry=...`.

Its field predicate follows direct envelopes, `$ref`, `allOf`, nested properties/arrays, receipt `full_value_request.event`, coordinator event references, the frozen 1.0.0 compatibility envelope, and every Storage-classified node in `Plans/event_datetime_inventory.json`, including envelopes with string-only identity declarations, frozen append inputs, original Storage fields, index rows and boot-recovery issued originals.
Selection uses the exact resource-content hash and reviewed field path, not a schema discriminator or timestamp-name guess.
It remains installed when a referenced resource declares `$schema`; the original resource objects/bytes, complete-document hashes and all schema predicates stay unchanged.
A stock validator on the broad source schema is insufficient.

At a separate scalar field boundary, including a reference to only a timestamp subschema, call `date_time(..., profile=STORAGE_UTC_Z)`; select `coordination_utc_z` only for its owner fields and `legacy_normalization_output` only for that output form.
Frozen SP-1101 verifiers construct this same outer boundary with the authenticated original resource map and field profiles; current request data never selects them.
statements.no_mutation: SP-1101 original selection is RetainedDispatcher in pm_event_numbers (number scope, its own rules table); the date-time code supplies only the profiles it selects, whose rules are profile.*.

statements.statement: This preserves broad original source timestamps while enforcing CV-253 on original Storage fields; skipped old format checks do not authorize invalid Storage history.
Preserve strings in hashes.

statements.statement: A newly declared UTC field, a removed node, resource drift, an unclassified entry or a changed owner citation fails until the inventory is reviewed.

statements.no_mutation: Ownership or governance statement; no date-time code implements it.

statements.statement: Resource admission runs before every evaluated schema object.

statements.statement: The static gate has a bounded universe: **every regular file under `Plans/`, any suffix or case, following file and directory symlinks**.

It decodes JSON/JSONL in UTF-8, UTF-16 or UTF-32 (with or without BOM), CommonMark fences, indented code and HTML blocks in Markdown/MDX, and recursively serialized JSON objects/arrays in string values.
JSON-shaped inline code is checked too; ordinary prose and inline field-name references outside code blocks are outside this container universe.
Unsupported declaration candidates, including wildcard `patternProperties`/`propertyNames` in YAML, HTML script blocks or malformed JSON, fail even without literal timestamp names.

A container that mentions either field literally or through JSON Unicode escapes and yields no classified declaration also fails unless its exact path/origin/content hash is in `scripts/pm_event_datetime_exclusions.json` with reason and citation.
Exclusions cover only cited non-runtime data or lineage, including code examples and quoted inventory evidence.
A parsed JSON Schema with `$schema` or `$id`, or a file referenced by another schema, can never be excluded.
The gate derives eligibility from the source graph before applying any content pin; changed content requires review.
Unreadable files, duplicate keys, broken symlinks, cycles and stale exclusions fail.
`propertyNames` references are conservatively classified even when a full resolver would exclude the names.
Before any runtime installation, the inventory is validated against `scripts/pm_event_datetime_inventory.schema.json`.
Structural fingerprints, field sets and `role_evidence` are recomputed from source.
Storage/EventRecord/index/issued-copy roles keep CV-253/CV-1101 evidence and cannot select `owner_schema`.
Every other named field cites its own source schema pointer and exact value constraint, following offline references/combinators to their type, format and pattern.
The gate derives that evidence independently; another field's quote or a sibling pointer fails.
Unformatted source fields retain their original types without acquiring a timestamp predicate.

Wildcard roles use the committed timestamp battery as a trigger through the same closed reference resolver, supported dialects, JSON Schema keywords and enforced date-time checker as runtime validation.
Each declared key is tested in its map context, including propertyNames and intersecting patternProperties.

A map earns automatic `wildcard_non_timestamp` only when it refuses every battery sample and every year-sweep timestamp, has no sibling dependency, has a static closure (below), and its value schema holds only positive paths, annotations and subschema-free assertions (three maps).
statements.note: The count (three maps) is committed data, checked by datetime_unit_committed_role_counts.

statements.statement: Eighteen maps are explicitly reviewed in `scripts/pm_event_datetime_roles.json`.
statements.no_mutation: A count of committed review records, not code; datetime_unit_committed_role_counts checks it and the gate recomputes every record's evidence.

statements.statement: Eight keep `wildcard_non_timestamp_role`: permission records, tab records and settled-effect records.
statements.no_mutation: A count of committed review records, not code; datetime_unit_committed_role_counts checks it and the gate requires each to decide the string.

statements.statement: Ten are explicit owner-schema observations (`other_owner_observation`), because their cited definitions do not decide the string: schema-resource strings, arbitrary graph payload, setting values, SafeRef values and safe parameter values.
statements.note: The count (ten) is committed data, checked by datetime_unit_committed_role_counts.

statements.statement: Role authority is an allowlist: a citation counts only through the value schema itself, `$ref` or `allOf`, or through `anyOf`/`oneOf` when every branch carries that citation.
`$dynamicRef` is not on the list, because an outer document can rebind its anchor.
Every other keyword routes to `wildcard_role_review_required` with no automatic credit, while graph discovery may still walk it.

A positive path proves conjunction only, so the cited definition must also decide the string: on its own, through the same closed resolver, it must refuse every battery timestamp, each of 16 fixed non-timestamp strings and each of 4,743 year-sweep timestamps fixed in code (every year 1970-2100 in the battery's separators, zones and fraction lengths, with the first and last second of each year, its leap day and every real leap second).
A description-only, member-only or implicit-true citation never authorizes a value.
A role also requires the real validator over the whole map to refuse every battery timestamp (`all_refused`); it is required outright, never inferred from the citation.

Non-timestamp credit, automatic or role, needs a static closure: every node the value can reach is 2020-12, the dialect of every committed Plans schema, with no other dialect declared at or above it, and no reachable node carries `$dynamicRef`, `$dynamicAnchor`, `$recursiveRef` or `$recursiveAnchor`.

A mixed-dialect or dynamic closure routes to `wildcard_role_review_required`, because jsonschema evaluates a node in the dialect it was reached under and an outer document can rebind a dynamic anchor; within a static closure a node behaves the same in every context that reaches it.
The 16 strings, the year sweep and the battery are finite, refusal-only tests: they can withhold credit, never grant it.
statements.note: Each of these tests appears only in a credit predicate; every weakening of one is a witnessed credit_predicate mutation.

statements.statement: Proven nodes that accept a battery timestamp and refuse all 16 fixed strings are recorded as `timestamp_only_nodes` evidence.
Each role cites its own resolved schema and is pinned to the exact source-value graph fingerprint.
A changed value or reference target makes that review stale; regenerating inventory evidence does not update the role pin.
Acceptance without such a review requires `other_owner_observation` and the exact FIX10 schema-node evidence.
Pattern spelling and arbitrary-string acceptance never determine the role.
Both non-timestamp classes carry no timestamp-profile assertion.
`profile: owner_schema` preserves original validation and installs no timestamp overlay.
The inventory records battery fingerprint, sample count, per-field acceptance counts, resolved value fingerprint and the explicit reviewed role where present.
The inventory exclusion pin is recomputed from the source-derived projection; refreshing a checksum cannot authorize false field evidence or classification.
Inventory fingerprints establish content identity, independently of the installing owner's current/frozen custody obligations.
statements.no_mutation: Ownership or governance statement; no date-time code implements it.

statements.statement: Timestamp grammar | EventRecord/CV-317/CV-1101 enforces RFC3339 source/family date-time; CV-253 binds Storage observed/persisted fields to uppercase-Z UTC.
Stricter local fields and legacy normalization output keep their owners.
